scenes.name: Lo-fi house
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: House casero de medios escasos que arrasa en internet entre una generación cuyo primer contacto con el house es esta música.

scenes.name: Grime rennaisance
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Tras años olvidado por el auge del dubstep, el grime regresa a mediados de los 2010 y se convierte en fenómeno pop.

scenes.name: Trap español y electrónica latina
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Subgénero del sur de EE UU (rimas en tríadas, TR-808, textura gótica) que en España encarnan Pxxr Gvng, Yung Beef, Kinder Malo, Pimp Flaco, Dellafuente o Cecilio G.: más vídeos de YouTube que discos. «No existe tanta diferencia entre un aficionado al trap y un fiestero de la Ruta del bakalao.» A su lado, el dancehall de Bad Gyal, el reggaetón experimental de Miss Nina o La Favi y el electrolatino de Juan Magán.

scenes.name: Neo-rave / revival de los noventa
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Regreso de los sonidos de los noventa (primer trance, rave de 1990-1993, hardcore europeo, gabber) por productores que no los vivieron: In Colour de Jamie xx, DJ Sports, las mixtapes Back to the Future de Paul Kalkbrenner, AraabMuzik, Evian Christ, Toxe.

scenes.name: Tropical house
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: House de playas, humedad y verano idealizado: el puente entre los ritmos del Caribe y Sudamérica y la escena comercial estadounidense.

scenes.name: Dancehall vs. pop
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: El pop comercial toma ahora como patrón el dancehall digital y futurista: riddims para engarzar las melodías más pegadizas.

scenes.name: Weightless grime
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Grime sin voces y sin peso: una caja y un bajo pulsante en cuyo espacio vacío ocurren acontecimientos inesperados.

scenes.name: Future bass
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: La estética digital de la EDM con subgraves monumentales: trap, dubstep y hip hop con la pegada y el brillo de neón del trance.

scenes.name: Ghetto-gothic / club mutante
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Código surgido en los clubes gays de Nueva York (las fiestas GHE20G0TH1K de Venus X): cuero sadomasoquista, negro gótico y una pulpa de techno, house, dubstep, electro y reggaetón en desintegración. Su gran figura es Arca (Xen, Mutant, Arca; productor de fka twigs y Björk), con Lotic, Rabit, Yves Tumor o Ziúr; la sexualidad como naturaleza indefinida.

scenes.name: Big room
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Lo que suena en la sala principal y los grandes escenarios de la EDM: house progresivo, trance y hardcore con decibelios y textura relampagueante.

scenes.name: Cloud rap
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Hip hop instrumental licuado en vapor: beats fungosos, bajos macizos y ambientes que provocan ensoñación, como estar tumbado en una nube. Conectado con el vaporwave por su nostalgia rencorosa y su vida al margen del circuito comercial, a golpe de mixtape.

scenes.name: Afrobeats
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Subgéneros urbanos del África subsahariana, dominantes en Angola o Ghana y producidos también en la diáspora europea.

scenes.name: Alt-R&B
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: La desviación indie y experimental del R&B, con préstamos del dubstep, el deep house y otros géneros recién llegados.

scenes.name: Deep house (2010s)
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: No confundir con el de los noventa: el house delicado lavado con texturas de electrohouse, EDM y post-dubstep que triunfó en Ibiza y medio mundo.

scenes.name: Drone techno
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: El hard techno se renueva con zumbidos amenazantes del industrial y el metal a tempo suave: textura metálica y cenicienta, el sonido de la crisis de Occidente.

scenes.name: Underground online
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Una generación que madura y se promociona en internet, lejos de la industria, con YouTube o Bandcamp.

scenes.name: Net concrète & nueva academia
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: La música concreta y la composición algorítmica reaparecen con la cultura de club de fondo e internet como medio: compleja y accesible a la vez.

scenes.name: Vaporwave
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Profundiza en la hipnagogia subrayando el futuro traicionado de la utopía tecnológica de los ochenta: una ensoñación que preludia una pesadilla.

scenes.name: Hipster house
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Músicos del indie-rock y el post-hardcore se entusiasman con los beats elásticos del house y crean música de club intuitiva y desastrada.

scenes.name: Outsider house / techno mutante
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Una región imprecisa del underground online que difumina las fronteras entre techno, house, ambient, dub, ruido y hasta rap: autoediciones, casetes y Bandcamp. Giegling (Traumprinz / Prince of Denmark), Diagonal (Powell), Opal Tapes (Huerco S.), Northern Electronics, L.I.E.S. de Ron Morelli, Lobster Theremin, Actress (Hazyville), Laurel Halo, Nicolas Jaar, Floating Points, Dean Blunt, patten.

scenes.name: Tribal mexicano / changa tuki
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Escenas locales de consumo autóctono: el tribal del norte de México, que electrifica rancheras y corridos (Javier Estrada), y el changa tuki de Caracas, folclore venezolano con bombo house y fogonazos de dubstep y trance (Pacheko, DJ Yirvin).

scenes.name: Xenomanía
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Artistas occidentales inspirados en armonías y tradiciones no occidentales: el equivalente electrónico al turismo selectivo.

scenes.name: Post-dubstep
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: El dubstep se abre al pop, los ritmos africanos, el techno y el house: no un género, sino un espacio de cambio y evolución.

scenes.name: Revival new age
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Con el regreso de los aparatos analógicos se reivindica la primera new age, la más próxima al ambient solemne de los setenta.

scenes.name: Electro-chaabi
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: La electrónica de los países de mayoría musulmana; nacido en Egipto, se expande por el norte de África y llega a Francia.

scenes.name: Abstract beatz
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: El hip hop abstracto en contacto con la IDM, el R&B y el dubstep alcanza un estado psicodélico y viajero, integrable con trap, house o EDM.

scenes.name: EDM
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Electronic dance music: la corriente más accesible y fronteriza con el pop, una renovación de la cultura rave al estilo superproducción de Hollywood.

scenes.name: Techno oscuro / post-industrial
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Tras el minimal, el techno vuelve a la fuerza y la oscuridad pero a menor tempo (120-130 bpm), con espacio para matices de dub, dubstep, IDM e industrial: refugio de la música de club intelectualizada frente a la EDM. Sandwell District (Regis, Function, Female, Silent Servant), Surgeon, el techno hipnótico de Donato Dozzy o Mike Parker y sellos como Semántica.

scenes.name: Bassline house
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Vuelta de tuerca al speed garage de 1997 con graves más musculosos, surgida en el norte de Inglaterra.

scenes.name: Synth-wave
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Incluye la minimal wave (el synth-pop doméstico y oscuro de los ochenta, recuperado arqueológicamente) y las imitaciones pulidas actuales para series y videojuegos.

scenes.name: Bandas sonoras electrónicas
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Se intensifica el vínculo entre cine y electrónica: bandas sonoras electrónicas en series y en Hollywood amenazan al lenguaje orquestal.

scenes.name: Nuevos analógicos
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Frente a la tiranía digital, se rescatan los sintetizadores de los setenta y regresa la estética de los orígenes de la música electrónica.

scenes.name: Techno Berghain
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: La guardia pretoriana de DJs de Berghain (Marcel Dettmann, Ben Klock) promueve un techno equidistante entre la dureza metálica y la ductilidad digital; arriba, en Panoramabar, un house luminoso y clásico (Prosumer, Nick Höppner). Control férreo en la puerta (Sven Marquardt) y prohibición de fotos.

scenes.name: Psy-trance
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Trance psicodélico heredero del goa trance: arpegios furiosos y veloces hacia el rapto místico; muy popular en Israel.

scenes.name: Electrocumbia
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: La cumbia en fase digital: baladas de acordeón con latidos de dub, dancehall y house. También «cumbia sonidera» o «rebajada».

scenes.name: Trap
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: El hip hop sureño del siglo XXI sobre delincuencia, cárcel y venta de droga, sobre bases sincopadas hechas sobre todo con la TR-808.

scenes.name: Detroit house
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: La nueva generación de Detroit conserva el aspecto emocional y soul de su ciudad, en contacto con el deep house, el jazz y la raíz negra.

scenes.name: Detroit 2.0
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Productores, sellos, tiendas y fans que conservan la elegancia y la textura sintética del techno original: no un revival, sino la conservación del techno «verdadero».

scenes.name: Indie-classical
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Compositores de formación clásica y minimalista atraídos por el ambient, la IDM, el indie-pop y el techno.

scenes.name: World music 2.0
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: No una escena sino un concepto: la world music pasa al paradigma digital y forma una red entre África, Sudamérica, Europa y Estados Unidos.

scenes.name: Revival acid / IDM ácida
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: La «technostalgia» por la TB-303: no un revival exacto sino la línea ácida retorcida a conveniencia por la IDM. «¿De verdad crees que el acid se había ido?» (Aphex Twin). Luke Vibert (YosepH, 2003), Ceephax Acid Crew, la serie Analord de AFX (2005), Atom™ y una nueva ola de acid house (Gerome Sportelli, Azari & III, Tin Man, Jesper Dahlbäck).

scenes.name: K-pop
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: La industria del pop surcoreano: artificioso, espectacular, reciclable y de alcance global. Su equivalente japonés es el J-pop.

scenes.name: Drone metal
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: El metal experimental (doom, black) adopta el lenguaje del dron: hipnosis, ambientes intoxicados y opresión cavernosa.

scenes.name: Drones
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Un zumbido que prolonga hasta el infinito una nota y sus modulaciones: la unidad básica del minimalismo convertida en género de escucha obsesiva.

scenes.name: Pop ambient
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Etiqueta del sello Kompakt que actualiza el ambient de los noventa: melodías sumergidas en un grueso colchón de texturas casi celestiales.

scenes.name: Hauntology
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Los recuerdos del pasado se infiltran en el sonido como fantasmas: un ejercicio de memoria nebulosa, una anticiencia ficción desoladora.

scenes.name: Footwork
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Evolución del ghetto house de Chicago que, sin su carga soez, queda en un esqueleto rítmico intrincado: música para los pies con vías experimentales.

scenes.name: Revival electro
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Los niños de Computer World y Planet Rock recuperan el electro y el synth-pop: New School Science de Jedi Knights (1996) fue el primer aviso; DMX Krew lo niega: «el electro nunca se fue». Patrick Pulsinger y Cheap en Viena; I-F y Viewlexx en La Haya, que rescatan el italodisco; sellos Schematic, Electron Industries.

scenes.name: Crunk y trap en Atlanta
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.desc: Lil Jon, A&R de So So Def, se convirtió con los East Side Boyz en la cara del crunk (Get Crunk, Who U Wit, 1997). En 1999 Def Jam ya no pudo ignorar el Sur y creó Def Jam South con Scarface al frente, que fichó a Chris Lova Lova, DJ de Hot 97.5 que vendía Incognegro desde el maletero: Ludacris (Back for the First Time, 2000). T.I., tras fracasar en Arista, se hizo fuerte con las mixtapes de DJ Drama, fundó Grand Hustle y con Trap Muzik (2003) llevó al gran público el trap, la música de la calle del trapicheo: sintetizadores, baterías potentes y charles nerviosos, con productores como DJ Toomp, Shawty Redd, Drumma Boy, Lex Luger o Zaytoven, cuyo piano hizo brillar a Gucci Mane (en un solo día de 2009 salieron «Bricks» y «Make Tha Trap Say Aye»). Luego Jeezy, Future, Migos, 21 Savage o Lil Baby: Atlanta, ciudad del fénix, destruye su sonido cada pocos años para crear otro.

scenes.name: Kwaito y house sudafricano
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Uno de los primeros sonidos de la Sudáfrica posapartheid, vinculado al house: DJ Mujava («Township Funk», Warp, 2008), el shangaan electro de DJ Nozinja, el deep house de Black Coffee o Culoe de Song y la performance zef de Die Antwoord.

scenes.name: Flamenco electrónico
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: La desafección entre electrónica y flamenco: la tecno-rumba de Camela es una actualización tecnológica de la rumba; Chambao populariza el flamenco chill. Lo más interesante: Enrique Morente con Carlos Jean o Domestic, y «Raverdial» (2017) de Los Voluble con Niño de Elche.

scenes.name: Hip hop español
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Nacido en los barrios cerca de las bases estadounidenses; Yo Gano publica a CPV (1994). 7 Notas 7 Colores lo saca del underground (1997); SFDK, La Mala Rodríguez (Lujo ibérico, flamenco y rap), Violadores del Verso, Sólo los Solo. Subsellos instrumentales (Tú Pierdes: trip-hop y abstract beats, Javi P3z) y de electro (Headspin, Alek Stark). Luego Rayden, El Coleta o C. Tangana.

scenes.name: Techno y club español (Sónar, SOMA, Moog, La Real)
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Sónar (1994; Ricard Robles, Sergio Caballero, Enric Palau) une música de baile y experimental, de día y de noche. En Madrid, Óscar Mulero (The Omen), SOMA y la revista Undersounds; recopilaciones Electronic Generators (Geometrik) y Disco 2000 (Cosmos). En Barcelona, Nitsa (Sideral, DJ Zero), Moog y Minifunk. Entre 1996 y 2002 «el techno se hizo masivo»: Florida 135 y el Groove Parade de Monegros, La Real de Oviedo y Gijón, Vademecum de Vigo. En el siglo XXI, sellos con distribución global: Factor City (Undo), Regular (Iñaki Marín), Net28 (Alex Under), Hivern Discs (John Talabot), Semántica (Svreca).

scenes.name: Reggaetón
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Dancehall en español nacido en Panamá y Puerto Rico; su variante pop deforma el riddim Dem Bow con melodías sencillas y alcance comercial incomparable.

scenes.name: Techno-dub
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: El dub de Jamaica se encuentra en Berlín con el techno de Detroit: sonido voluble e hipnótico de bajos pulsantes.

scenes.name: Funk carioca
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Deformación del ritmo roto del electro con ritmos brasileños como la samba, fraguada en las favelas de Río y lanzada a la escena global a principios de siglo.

scenes.name: Dance-pop
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.desc: Remixes y productores de house, techno o hip hop dan al pop independiente una pátina electrónica y un pulso bailable.

scenes.name: Jay-Z y Roc-A-Fella
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.desc: Shawn Carter aprendió con Jaz-O y recorrió las giras de Big Daddy Kane; DJ Clark Kent, convencido de que era «el Jesucristo del rap», dejó dos sellos que no quisieron ficharlo, le montó un estudio en casa y le presentó a Damon Dash, que defendía a su Big L. Con Dash y Kareem «Biggs» Burke fundó Roc-A-Fella (1995) para ser independiente. Reasonable Doubt (1996), rap mafioso de un buscavidas que reflexiona sobre esa vida («D’Evils», «Regrets»), con DJ Premier, Clark Kent, Ski Beatz («Dead Presidents», sobre Lonnie Liston Smith y una frase de Nas) y «Brooklyn’s Finest» con Biggie, que no podía creer que Jay no escribiera las rimas: se convirtieron en rivales y amigos. Iba a ser un solo disco; acabó con catorce números 1, Rocawear, la presidencia de Def Jam y el primer billón del hip hop. Roc-A-Fella, con Just Blaze, Kanye West, Beanie Sigel, Cam’ron, Memphis Bleek o Dipset bajo el mismo techo, se vendió a Island Def Jam en 2004.

scenes.name: El fin del sampleo libre y el oficio del productor
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.desc: Transformar lo que existía en algo nuevo está en la base del hip hop: de los breaks de los pioneros a la caja de Marley Marl, el muro de la Bomb Squad y los collages de jazz de De La Soul, Tribe, Pete Rock o DJ Premier. Nadie pensaba en derechos hasta que el rap dio dinero. En diciembre de 1991 Gilbert O’Sullivan ganó a Biz Markie por samplear «Alone Again (Naturally)» sin permiso (250.000 dólares y la retirada del disco); De La Soul pactó con los Turtles. Biz llamó a su siguiente disco All Samples Cleared! y el salvaje Oeste se acabó: a los productores de Rush les dieron una lista de artistas intocables, y Easy Mo Bee empezó a samplear instrumentos sueltos y tocar encima («Flava in Ya Ear»). «La cultura negra siempre recibe las sobras y las convierte en lo que lo controla todo» (Salaam Remi). El productor es también psiquiatra y entrenador; hoy se hace un éxito con un portátil, y algunos, como Timbaland regalándole su archivo de sonidos a Just Blaze, rompieron la costumbre de tapar las etiquetas.

scenes.name: Grammys, Óscars, Hall of Fame y el Pulitzer
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.desc: Los grandes premios rechazaron o reconocieron tarde al hip hop. En los Grammy de 1984, la noche de Thriller, Herbie Hancock tocó «Rockit» con Grand Mixer D.ST en los platos: para Paradise Gray, la primera vez que se vio en la tele. En 1989 se creó el Grammy al mejor rap pero se entregó fuera de la retransmisión: Def Jam y Rush encabezaron el boicot y DJ Jazzy Jeff & the Fresh Prince no fueron a recoger el premio por «Parents Just Don’t Understand»; Kool Moe Dee sí fue, harto de que nadie hablara de estrategia («¿no decíamos que nos importaba un carajo el Grammy?»). En 1990 Young MC lo ganó en directo a «Fight the Power» y Flavor Flav le asaltó el escenario. Eminem fue el primer rapero en ganar un Óscar con «Lose Yourself» (2003, con Luis Resto), y Three 6 Mafia el segundo; Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five entraron los primeros en el Rock and Roll Hall of Fame (2007). En 2014 Macklemore se disculpó con Kendrick Lamar por ganarle; en 2018 DAMN. de Lamar, criado en Top Dawg por Punch, ganó el Pulitzer, algo que Nation of Millions habría merecido treinta años antes.

scenes.name: Escribir rimas: libretas, cabezas y negros
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.desc: Desde Rakim, KRS-One y Kane, la lírica es un arte competitivo: unos escriben en libretas, otros en el móvil en un atasco, otros, como Biggie, Jay-Z o Styles P, en la cabeza. Para unos hay que «dejar joyas» y enseñar (Chuck D: «no rimo por rimar»); para otros basta con que suene bien sobre la base. Cormega tira nueve de cada diez rimas; K-Rino dice que el bloqueo es falta de lecturas; Bruce Lee y las diez mil horas. El negro (ghostwriting) existe desde que Caz rapeó sin saberlo en «Rapper’s Delight»: Kane escribía para la Juice Crew, The D.O.C. y Eminem para Dr. Dre, y Meek Mill acusó a Drake; para unos traiciona la autenticidad, para otros es como Al Pacino haciendo de cubano.

scenes.name: El hip hop: medio siglo de historia oral
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.desc: Un género nacido de la imaginación de chavales abandonados entre las ruinas del Bronx de los setenta que sobrevivió a todo (a una generación mayor que lo rechazaba, a las radios que no lo ponían, a los políticos que lo atacaban) hasta convertirse en la música más popular de Estados Unidos. Abrams hizo más de trescientas entrevistas entre 2018 y 2022 a DJs, artistas, productores, ejecutivos y periodistas para contar su origen y su expansión: del Bronx a los demás distritos «como las venas de un plano del metro», del parque al vinilo, a la Costa Oeste con el gangsta rap y el G-funk, al Sur y más allá. «La lírica es, al fin y al cabo, una forma de tradición oral.»

facts.title: Nostalgia Boom for Older Acts (2016 onward)
facts.body: The "Concert Nostalgia Boom" reflects a resurgence of interest in "heritage acts" or "legacy bands" from the 1960s, 70s, and 80s, who began touring again to very large audiences. Fans are willing to pay significant amounts to see these classic artists, driven by a desire to relive their youth. Promoters like Live Nation and AEG increasingly rely on these older acts to fill arenas and stadiums, as the recorded music industry has struggled to create a similar number of new stadium-filling artists. "Fans want to see these classic artists while they still can, and they're willing to pay for the privilege."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 4: (70-61)

facts.title: Death in 2016
facts.body: David Bowie was among the musicians whose passing in 2016 contributed to a perceived new era in rock history where many beloved artists began to die off. "That one year we lost David Bowie."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: In Memoriam of Those Lost in 2022
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Death from Liver Cancer (2016)
facts.body: David Bowie ultimately passed away from liver cancer on January 16, 2016. "Liver Cancer eventually took down David Bowie on January 16th, 2016."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Death and Public Reaction (2016)
facts.body: David Bowie died suddenly and surprisingly from cancer in 2016, a fact that was initially met with disbelief and led to weeks of global mourning. His death was unexpected as he had released a critically acclaimed surprise album in 2013 and another acclaimed album just three days before his passing. "David Bowie had suddenly, surprisingly, passed away."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: January 10, 2016 - Passing Away
facts.body: David Bowie passed away on January 10th, 2016, just two days after his 69th birthday. His death marked the end of a career that spanned six decades and profoundly influenced music and culture. "David Bowie, who passed away on January 10th, 2016, just two days after his 69th birthday."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Death and Health Battle (2016)
facts.body: David Bowie passed away on January 16, 2016. He had been dealing with various health issues, including a heart attack, for approximately twelve years. In mid-2014, he was secretly diagnosed with liver cancer, which had a poor prognosis and indicated his time was limited. "the death of David Bowie on January 16th, 2016."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 10: (10-1)
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Death in 2016
facts.body: David Bowie was among the notable rock stars who passed away in 2016, a year characterized by an unusual number of significant losses in the music world. "David Bowie, Prince, Glen Fry of the Eagles, two members of the Jefferson Airplane, Matt Roberts of Three Doors Down, George Michael, Beatles producer George Martin, Keith Emerson and Greg Lake of Emerson, like in Palmer, Maurice White of Earth Wind and Fire and dozens more."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 7: (40-31)
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Death (January 10, 2016)
facts.body: David Bowie died on January 10, 2016, a death that marked a grim realization about the aging of music heroes. He had been quietly battling liver cancer. "It was with his death on January 10, 2016 that the hard truth about our aging heroes really began to set in."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 2: The Role of Indie Rock
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Death Announcement Shock (January 10, 2016)
facts.body: David Bowie's death on January 10, 2016, stunned the public, who widely perceived him as an immortal, eternal, and ever-evolving figure. "When David Bowie died on January 10, 2016, everybody was stunned. I mean, this is Bowie. Bowie wasn't supposed to die."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Blackstar Release on 69th Birthday (January 8, 2016)
facts.body: Bowie's final album, "Blackstar," was released on Friday, January 8, 2016, coinciding with his 69th birthday. That same night, Holy Holy, a band featuring some of his former Spiders from Mars backing musicians, played a show in New York City, and while there was speculation Bowie might appear, he did not; instead, the band left him a voicemail with the crowd singing "Happy Birthday." "On Friday, January 18, the day Blackstar, that album he'd been working on during his illness, was released, and it was also Bowie's 69th birthday."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Death at Home (January 10, 2016)
facts.body: David Bowie passed away on Sunday, January 10, 2016, at his home, surrounded by his family. "And then on Sunday, the story is that he laid down at his home, surrounded by his family, and died."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Death and Diagnosis (January 11, 2016)
facts.body: David Bowie died at 2:30 in the morning of Monday, January 11, 2016, due to liver cancer. His illness had been diagnosed approximately 18 months prior to his passing, a fact kept largely private from the public. "Bowie was gone, a victim of liver cancer that had been diagnosed about 18 months earlier."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Death and Posthumous Arrangements (2016)
facts.body: David Bowie died peacefully in his sleep at his New York home on Sunday, January 10, 2016, at the age of 69, after an 18-month battle with cancer, having released his final album *Blackstar* just two days prior on his birthday. His death was confirmed by his publicist and son, Duncan Jones, leading to a massive global outpouring of tributes, including 20,000 tweets a minute within an hour. As per his instructions, there was no funeral; he was cremated, and his ashes were taken to Bali for Buddhist rituals, though the exact location where they were spread (possibly Alma Pura or the Sidemen fields, places he loved) remains unknown. "He hung on until this last album was released and his birthday. And then after that, his job was done."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: David Bowie's Death (January 10, 2016)
facts.body: David Robert Jones, known as David Bowie, died at the age of 69 on January 10th, 2016, two days after the release of his final album, "Blackstar." Producer Tony Visconti described "Blackstar" as Bowie's "parting gift" to the world. "Two days later, on January 10th, 2016, David Robert Jones, aka David Bowie, died at the age of 69."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Posthumous Chart Success (2016)
facts.body: The week after Bowie's death, his final album "Blackstar" debuted at number one on the Billboard 200, impressively knocking Adele's "25" from the top spot, becoming America's "parting gift" to him. On the Hot 100, "Lazarus" debuted at number 40 (his last US Top 40 hit), and classic hits "Space Oddity" and "Under Pressure" re-entered at numbers 42 and 45. Twenty-one Bowie songs, including seven from "Blackstar" and 14 greatest hits, debuted on Billboard's Hot Rock and Alternative Songs Chart, taking up more than half of its top 20. facts.title: Death and Posthumous Arrangements (2016)
facts.body: David Bowie died peacefully in his sleep at his New York home on Sunday, January 10, 2016, at the age of 69, after an 18-month battle with cancer, having released his final album *Blackstar* just two days prior on his birthday. His death was confirmed by his publicist and son, Duncan Jones, leading to a massive global outpouring of tributes, including 20,000 tweets a minute within an hour. As per his instructions, there was no funeral; he was cremated, and his ashes were taken to Bali for Buddhist rituals, though the exact location where they were spread (possibly Alma Pura or the Sidemen fields, places he loved) remains unknown. "He hung on until this last album was released and his birthday. And then after that, his job was done."

facts.title: Oasis Reunion Speculation and Supersonic Premiere (2016)
facts.body: The English press occasionally reported on a potential Oasis reunion, citing reasons such as Liam's financial needs or their mother Peggy's desire for reconciliation. At the October 2016 London premiere of the Oasis documentary "Supersonic," Liam attended, but Noel was absent. Liam publicly remarked on Noel's absence, sarcastically suggesting he was in one of his "really big houses" having a "face peel." Despite the snipes, Liam also expressed openness to a reunion at this time. "In October 2016, the Oasis documentary Super Sonic had its premiere in London. Liam was there, but Noel wasn't."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Liam's Ambivalence Towards Reunion (2016)
facts.body: At the premiere of the Oasis documentary "Supersonic" in October 2016, Liam Gallagher acknowledged that it was good for people to be speaking about Oasis again, but he did not believe a reunion would result from the documentary or ongoing discussions. He cited his and Noel's busy schedules as a practical impediment. "I think it is good that people are speaking about Oasis, so I'll agree, but not about just being actually having a little bit of sheep and bigs at each other. So I think that's good that people are sort of speaking about us as a band again. But I don't think much of you're going to come from it."

facts.body: The band played their final show on August 20, 2016, in Kingston, their hometown. facts.body: The band announced the "Man-Machine Poem" tour on May 25, 2016, the day after Dr. James Perry publicly announced Gord Downie's incurable brain tumor. facts.body: On May 24, 2016, a press conference revealed that Gord Downie, the band's beloved singer, had been diagnosed with glioblastoma, a highly aggressive and incurable form of brain cancer, following a seizure. The news deeply shocked Canada, where the band had become widely recognized as "Canada's house band." "On May 24, 2016, a press conference was held. Gord Downey, the hip's beloved singer, had been diagnosed with glioblastoma, a very aggressive form of brain cancer after he had a seizure."

The Canadian Prime Minister also attended this historic event. "And the final show was officially watched by 11 million people in a country with about 35 million people."

facts.title: Man Machine Poem Tour (2016) - National Celebration
facts.body: Following Gord Downie's diagnosis, The Tragically Hip embarked on the Man Machine Poem Tour in 2016. This tour quickly transformed into a national celebration of Gord, the band, rock music, and Canadian identity. The final show, broadcast on a Saturday night in August, was watched by tens of millions of Canadians, bringing the country to a standstill. "that same news conference also announced that the hip was going on tour again, the man machine poem tour. That turned into a national celebration of all things. Gord, all things hip, all things rock, and all things Canadian. Tens of millions of people stop what they were doing and watch the final show that Saturday night and August."

facts.title: "Man-Machine Poem" Tour Announcement (2016)
facts.body: The band announced the "Man-Machine Poem" tour on May 25, 2016, the day after Dr. James Perry publicly announced Gord Downie's incurable brain tumor. This announcement initially led many fans into a state of denial regarding Gord's health. "But we didn't have that much time to absorb everything because one day later, the hip announced the man-machine poem tour."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Tragically Hip

facts.title: Final Concert Broadcast (2016)
facts.body: The band's final show in Kingston was officially watched by 11 million people across Canada, a country with approximately 35 million inhabitants. The true viewership number is estimated to be at least twice that, factoring in the numerous mass listening and watching parties held nationwide and globally. The Canadian Prime Minister also attended this historic event. "And the final show was officially watched by 11 million people in a country with about 35 million people."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 10: (10-1)
facts.name: The Tragically Hip

facts.title: Final Cross-Canada Tour (2016)
facts.body: Despite Downie's severe health challenges, The Tragically Hip announced and undertook one final cross-Canada tour. It commenced on July 22 in Victoria and concluded with a poignant hometown performance in Kingston on August 20. This tour was regarded as the most emotional musical tour Canada had ever experienced. "the hip announced one final cross-Canada tour, starting on July 22, in Victoria, and ending with the hometown show in Kingston on August 20."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 10: (10-1)
facts.name: The Tragically Hip

facts.title: Final Show (August 20, 2016)
facts.body: The band played their final show on August 20, 2016, in Kingston, their hometown. During this concert, Gord Downie notably called out the then-Prime Minister, who was present, to address the longstanding issues facing Canada's Indigenous people. "When the hit played their final show on August 20, 2016 in Kingston, Gord called out the Prime Minister by name who was there, suddenly demanding, okay, not so subtly, that he'd deal with these longstanding problems."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Tragically Hip

facts.title: Gord Downie's Cancer Diagnosis (2016)
facts.body: On May 24, 2016, a press conference revealed that Gord Downie, the band's beloved singer, had been diagnosed with glioblastoma, a highly aggressive and incurable form of brain cancer, following a seizure. The news deeply shocked Canada, where the band had become widely recognized as "Canada's house band." "On May 24, 2016, a press conference was held. Gord Downey, the hip's beloved singer, had been diagnosed with glioblastoma, a very aggressive form of brain cancer after he had a seizure."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 10: (10-1)
facts.name: The Tragically Hip

facts.title: Gord Downie's Cancer Diagnosis (2016)
facts.body: In 2016, Gord Downie was diagnosed with glioblastoma, an aggressive and terminal form of brain cancer, with a prognosis of one to five years of survival. "Gordowning was dying. Brain cancer. Something called glioblastoma. The prognosis wasn't good. The condition was terminal. One year, maybe two, five, at best."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Tragically Hip

facts.title: Honorary Degrees from Queen's University (2016)
facts.body: In 2016, the band members received honorary degrees from their alma mater, Queen's University in Kingston, where three of them had been students. "And in 2016 the hip received honorary degrees from their alma mater, Queen's University in Kingston."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Tragically Hip

facts.title: "Man-Machine Poem" Tour Announcement (2016)
facts.body: Following Gord Downie's diagnosis, The Tragically Hip embarked on the Man Machine Poem Tour in 2016. This tour quickly transformed into a national celebration of Gord, the band, rock music, and Canadian identity. The final show, broadcast on a Saturday night in August, was watched by tens of millions of Canadians, bringing the country to a standstill. "that same news conference also announced that the hip was going on tour again, the man machine poem tour. That turned into a national celebration of all things. Gord, all things hip, all things rock, and all things Canadian. Tens of millions of people stop what they were doing and watch the final show that Saturday night and August."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Tragically Hip

facts.title: National Outpouring of Affection (2016)
facts.body: The Tragically Hip received a "national outpouring of affection in the summer of 2016," demonstrating the strong pride Canadians have for their homegrown talent. "Just look at the national outpouring of affection for the tragically hip in the summer of 2016."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Tragically Hip

facts.title: Never Rehearsed for Tours (Pre-2016)
facts.body: Prior to Gord Downie's final tour in 2016, The Tragically Hip had never rehearsed for a tour. The severity of Gord's condition necessitated this change for the "Man-Machine Poem" tour. "The hip had never, ever rehearsed for a tour, but this time they had to."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Tragically Hip

facts.title: Rapid Ticket Sell-Out (2016)
facts.body: Tickets for the "Man-Machine Poem" tour went on sale on June 3, 2016, and sold out across the country within minutes, demonstrating immense public demand. "Tickets went on sale June 3rd and sold out across the country in minutes."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Tragically Hip

facts.title: Summer 2016 Tour Demand
facts.body: The Tragically Hip's tour in the summer of 2016 saw an immense disparity between ticket supply and demand. Only 200,000 tickets were available for sale, yet 4 million people attempted to purchase them. This massive imbalance inevitably led to widespread disappointment among fans who were unable to secure tickets. "There were 200,000 tickets available, but 4 million people tried to buy them."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Tragically Hip

facts.title: Surgery and Post-Surgical Prognosis (2016)
facts.body: In early 2016, surgeon Douglas DJ Cook at Kingston General Hospital performed a full temporal lobectomy, removing Gord's left temporal lobe, hippocampus, and additional tissue. The best-case scenario after surgery was 4-5 years without further neurological decline. "His surgeon was Douglas DJ Cook at Kingston General Hospital. Dr. Cook went in and removed Gord's left temporal lobe. This is called a full temporal abectomy."

facts.title: Radiation and Chemotherapy (2016)
facts.body: Following surgery, Gord underwent 30 rounds of radiation treatment over six weeks, twice a day, five days a week. This was supplemented by an oral chemotherapy drug called Tilosilamide. His brother Pat accompanied him, playing music, including The Bee Gees, during treatments. "After the surgery came 30 rounds of radiation treatment. Twice a day, five days a week for six weeks. He would go in for treatment with his brother Pat who would play music for Gord."

facts.name: Gord Downie

facts.title: Incurable Tumor Announcement (2016)
facts.body: On May 24, 2016, Dr. James Perry of Sunnybrook Hospital publicly announced that Gord Downie's brain tumor was incurable, news that profoundly shocked Canada. "Good morning. My name is James Perry and I'm the head of the Division of Neurology here at Sunnybrook Hospital. I want to thank you for your attention and your concern in light of the difficult news that you all received this morning. It's my difficult duty today to tell you that Gord Downey's spring tumour is incurable."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Gord Downie

facts.title: Aaron Solowoniuk's MS Relapse and Album Absence (2016)
facts.body: On January 15, 2016, Aaron announced on YouTube that he was experiencing an MS relapse, which had been slowing him down for six to seven months. The symptoms made it difficult to perform daily tasks and play drums. He decided to step away from recording drums for the "Afraid of Heights" album to focus on his health, as he was unsure how long his recovery would take. The band fully supported his decision and brought in Jordan Hastings as a fill-in drummer.
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 3
facts.name: Billy Talent

facts.title: Band Support for Aaron Solowoniuk and FUMS (2016)
facts.body: Billy Talent, their management, and their record label (Warner Music Canada) are 100% supportive of Aaron in his struggle with MS. They established a charity called FUMS (Fuck U MS) to raise money for MS research. At a music festival on May 29, 2016, a band member (Ben Kowalewicz) addressed the crowd, expressing the band's love, care, and commitment to Aaron, and thanking Jordan Hastings for filling in. The speaker referred to Aaron as "Mr. A. S. Lua," which appears to be a mis-transcription of his full name, Aaron Solowoniuk.
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Billy Talent In Their Own Words: Part 3
facts.name: Billy Talent

facts.title: Unforeseen Rock am Ring Show (2016)
facts.body: During a Rock am Ring Festival performance in 2016, bad weather and lightning strikes led to the evacuation of the grounds. The band was initially told they wouldn't play, with headliners Deftones and Red Hot Chili Peppers scheduled before them. Unexpectedly, the Red Hot Chili Peppers requested that Billy Talent go on after them, resulting in Billy Talent headlining. The next day, the festival was canceled due to weather. This was Jordan Hastings' third show with the band, with his first two having been in Russia.
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Relapse and Stepping Back from Recording (January 15, 2016)
facts.body: In a YouTube message posted on January 15, 2016, Aaron Solowoniuk announced he was experiencing an MS relapse that had slowed him down over the past 6-7 months, making even simple tasks like climbing stairs daunting and drumming very tiring. Due to his health, he decided he couldn't play drums on the band's upcoming record and needed to focus on getting healthy. "On January 15th, 2016, Aaron posted a message on YouTube. facts.title: Stepping Back from Recording Drums (2016)
facts.body: On January 15, 2016, Aaron Solowoniuk announced via YouTube that he would temporarily step away from recording drums for Billy Talent's upcoming album due to an MS relapse. He explained that his symptoms were slowing him down, and he needed to focus on his health, expressing uncertainty about the duration of his recovery. "I'm not going to be able to play drums on this record. I just need to focus on my health while the record is being recorded."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
